title: Swap the blown fuse in a named DIN-rail fuse holder for the right rating
instruction: The panel is de-energized. Open fuse holder F2 (CONTROL XFMR), take out its blown fuse (marked with a black X) and drop it in the blue parts tray, put in the spare fuse whose rating matches the F2 legend (legends and spare labels are colour-coded by rating), and close the holder. Do not open F1 or F3.
context: Replacing blown control-circuit fuses is routine work for electricians (SOC 47-2111), industrial machinery mechanics (49-9041) and general maintenance and repair workers (49-9071): when a machine's control transformer or power supply loses its fuse, the panel is isolated, the blown cartridge is swapped for one of the rating printed on the holder's legend, and the machine is returned to service. The skill is in the details a hurried worker gets wrong: picking the spare whose rating matches the legend (a higher-rated fuse no longer protects the transformer or its wiring), opening only the named holder (a neighbouring carrier feeds another circuit, here the PLC supply or the cabinet light), and pushing the carrier fully home so the circuit is not left dead or intermittent. A robot that does this reliably takes over a frequent, low-variety maintenance call that today needs a trip by a qualified worker.
setup: Positions are measured forward from the line joining the two arm bases (61 cm apart), left or right of their midline as seen from behind the robot, and up from the table top. Back pan: a light-grey 3 mm steel plate (24 cm wide, 2 to 26 cm above the table) is centred on the midline, its front face 33.0 cm in front of the bases, held upright by a grey foot (20 x 10 x 2 cm) behind it that is fixed to the table. A steel EN 60715 TS35 x 7.5 DIN rail (20 cm long) runs across it, centre 14.9 cm above the table. Holders: three Eaton Bussmann CHM1DU one-pole modular fuse holders for 10 x 38 mm fuses (17.5 mm wide, 73.9 mm tall, 52.8 mm deep; grey plastic with a red grip tab at the top that stands 9 mm proud of the carrier face) clip on the rail, one blank 17.5 mm module between neighbours (35 mm centre to centre). F1 is centred 3.5 cm left of the midline, F2 on the midline, F3 3.5 cm right; their carrier front faces are 27.0 cm in front of the bases and their bottoms 11.0 cm above the table, so the grip tabs' tops are 17.1 cm up. Each fuse carrier hinges about a horizontal left-right axis 2.95 cm above the holder's bottom and 4 mm behind its face, and swings forward and down to a stop at 72 degrees; all three are latched shut. F2 holds a Bussmann KTK-6 fuse with a black marker X across its printed tube (the blown one); F1 and F3 each hold a fuse. Legends: above each holder a white plate (30 x 25 mm) on a small bracket off the pan, leaning back 45 degrees, its lower edge 19.2 cm above the table and 1.8 cm in front of the pan, carries the tag and circuit in black and the rating in white on a coloured lower half: 'F1 / PLC 24V DC / 2 A' on pink, 'F2 / CONTROL XFMR / 6 A' on green, 'F3 / CABINET LIGHT / 10 A' on red. Spares: a Bussmann KTK-10 and a KTK-6 10 x 38 mm midget fuse (10.3 mm across, 38.1 mm long, grey-white tube with plated end caps, rating printed along the tube; 9 g) lie on a dark-grey plastic stand, each in its own cradle (a post with low side lips; the fuse's axis 14.5 cm above the table) with the rating facing up, axis pointing forward from 23.2 to 27.0 cm in front of the bases, against an end stop at the far end. The KTK-10 is 9 cm right of the midline, the KTK-6 13 cm right. On the table in front of each cradle (22.4 to 24.6 cm in front of the bases, 2.8 cm wide, 4 mm high) is a rating label: '10 A' on red and '6 A' on green. Tray: a blue plastic parts tray (9 x 9 cm inside, 2.5 cm walls) sits on the table centred 20.5 cm in front of the bases and 20.5 cm right of the midline. Both arms start at the ready pose with their grippers open. One fixed layout, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Milestones: 0.25 F2's carrier is opened more than 30 degrees; 0.5 then the marked (blown) fuse is out of the carrier (its centre 25 mm or more from where it sat); 0.75 then the KTK-6 spare is seated in F2's carrier (centre within 2 mm of the seat, axis within 6 degrees of the carrier's); 1.0 then, after the check below, F2 is shut (within 1 degree) with the KTK-6 seated in it, the marked fuse rests inside the tray's walls, and the carrier held; if any 1.0 condition fails, no more than 0.75. After-release check, done once both grippers have been at least 6 cm from F2's grip tab for 1 s: hook a spring scale on F2's grip tab and pull it straight out toward the robot with 4 N (0.11 N m about the hinge) for 1.5 s. It passes if the carrier opens less than 3 degrees. Then open F2 and confirm that the fuse in it reads KTK-6 and carries no X. Hazards: the score is 0 for the whole trial, from the moment either of these happens, even if milestones were already reached or are reached afterwards: the F1 or F3 carrier opens 5 degrees or more; the KTK-10 is seated in F2's carrier (same seat test as above). Without a hazard, the score is the highest milestone reached. Dropping a fuse is not penalised by itself.
run_limit: 3,200 steps (160 s at 20 Hz); the scripted demo finishes in 1,952 steps (98 s)
reset_notes: Open F2, take out the KTK-6 and put the X-marked fuse back in its carrier, then push F2 shut until it latches. Lay the KTK-6 back in the far-right cradle and the KTK-10 in the other, both rating up and against the end stop. Check that F1 and F3 are latched shut. About 1.5 minutes.
fidelity: PhysX rigid bodies on joints, arms with the station's i2rt gains. Published: CHM1DU size and tab, 10 x 38 mm fuse; hinge and 72° opening read from Bussmann's drawing. Inferred: fuse lifts out of a U clip (internals unpublished); latch and open detent are joint springs (0.14-0.20 N·m, set to what the robot can open). Holders one module apart for the fingers; blown fuse marked with an X; rating colour codes; box colliders; pull test in sim after recording. Details in README.
